query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[3] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[4] (about=Lena, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:18:00) so basically the themed snack thing is actually a nice warm-up ritual tbh, it sets the tone before the game even starts. one could argue it's part of the social contract of game night
[5] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:11:00) Oath has a learning curve that would eat the whole evening. In my experience, new members need something with a shorter rules overhead first. Perhaps we revisit it when everyone has a baseline.
[6] (about=Felix, core, t8 @2026-03-23T19:01:00) Feels the group cares about games as games, not just the social aspect, unlike meetup nights.
[7] (about=Kezia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Wants to pitch a social deduction game for the marathon with a big group.
[8] (about=Lena, core, t0 @2026-03-02T19:00:00) Views themed snacks as a warm-up ritual that sets the tone and is part of the social contract of game night.
[9] (about=GROUP, said_by=Lena, group-insight, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) The norm is that everyone brings something (game or food) to the marathon; even those who brought nothing last year understood the expectation but didn't follow through.
[10] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Explains she did not want to interrupt the game, hence not mentioning the food issue.
[11] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement.
[12] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Bring-something rule for marathon: bring a game or food, both ideal; enforcement via social pressure.
[13] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Food for round two to be decided; Raj brought more flatbreads.
agent_answer:
**A. Nadia**

Nadia approaches the contribution norm differently: she **will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement**. She also explained she did not want to interrupt the game, so she did not mention the food issue. The broader group norm is stated as “bring a game or bring food,” but Nadia’s actual practice is to contribute on the game side only, not the food side.
